title: Ham or pork with potatoes and gravy

content.title: About
content.content: A classic dish of baked ham or boiled pork served with boiled or roasted potatoes and a rich meat gravy. The combination of tender meat, soft potatoes, and savory sauce makes it a staple for family meals and festive tables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ham is traditionally made from the hind leg of a pig and often smoked, giving it a distinctive flavor.
Gravy can be prepared from meat stock, cream, or tomato base, depending on regional preferences.
The dish is frequently accompanied by a side of green peas or pickled vegetables for contrast.
In some cuisines the potatoes are baked together with the meat, creating a crispy crust.
Adding onions and carrots to the gravy enhances its natural sweetness.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Ham and pork provide complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Energy‑providing carbs
items.content: Potatoes supply complex carbohydrates that release energy slowly, helping to maintain satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat is rich in thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Ham and pork contain iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Fiber from potatoes
items.content: When potatoes are served with the skin on, they add dietary fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham is often cured with salt; people with hypertension should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Pork contains saturated fats that can raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to pork proteins.

items.title: Spoilage risk
items.content: Meat and gravy can spoil quickly above 4 °C; store promptly in the refrigerator.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve hot, arranging slices of ham or pieces of pork beside boiled or roasted potatoes. Drizzle the whole plate with generous gravy and garnish with fresh herbs such as parsley or dill.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers to room temperature, then place in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in the oven or on the stovetop, adding a splash of stock if the gravy has thickened.
